parallel.requirements: Recognized the missing C++ header, black-box reference binary, exact five-line 29-byte output, std-only Cargo project, root test5.rs, module split, dual rustc/cargo buildability, and argv invariance.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent delegated a multi-phase workflow: three read-only analysts, an architect spec, one implementer with exclusive /output ownership, four read-only verifiers, optional fixer, and critic. Packaging analysis was retried twice after stalls.
parallel.implementation: The implementer wrote Cargo.toml, test5.rs, and format/progress_builder/progress_tracker modules, using f32 ratio math, formatted percentages, ProgressBuilder and ProgressTracker structs, and std::env::args collection.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was centralized in the implementer child, which wrote directly to /output and verified both rustc and cargo artifacts; artifact validation copied the expected files even though the parent never delivered a final response.
parallel.verification: Analysts and implementer ran reference, rustc, cargo, diff/cmp, byte count, and metadata checks. Four adversarial verifier children started, but the workflow was killed before their structured aggregate results, fix pass, or critic.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The code artifact passed the official evaluator, but the workflow status was killed, result null, final response empty, and verifier/critic lifecycle unfinished; a verifier observed a non-UTF-8 argv panic that official tests did not exercise.

serial.requirements: Recognized the missing header and black-box nature, the exact required output, pure Rust/std-only constraints, dual build paths, module organization, root test5.rs, and argv ignoring behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned the whole pipeline locally: probe the binary, implement modules and Cargo manifest, build, fix failures, run tests and byte comparisons, and report final caveats.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote format, builder, tracker, mod.rs, test5.rs, and Cargo.toml, then edited module re-exports and unused accessors after rustc and warning feedback.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were integrated in one workspace loop; rustc and cargo artifacts were produced under /output and the agent produced a final user-facing summary.
serial.verification: Serial ran binary probes, C++/Rust rounding comparisons, rustc and cargo builds, cargo tests, byte-for-byte comparisons across argument sets, and dependency/structure checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed. The final response disclosed untested ordinary choices around division by zero and defaults, but these did not affect the evaluated test.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow script restated exact output, no external crates, root test5.rs, module layout, dual build paths, and argv handling.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial prompt and final response show it handled the same required output, build paths, modules, std-only rule, and argv behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference for the official task; parallel additionally encoded the requirements into child briefs and a spec.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into analysts, architect, implementer, verifiers, fixer, and critic, with a single child owning /output implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in the main agent and performed probing, implementation, fixing, verification, and final summary itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit staged ownership and child boundaries; serial had no delegation and no retry handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried the same ground-truth requirements, but stalled packaging retries were restarted with the original broad brief rather than inherited checkpoints from prior attempts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained its own discovered context in one conversation, diagnosed rustc/import and warning issues, and edited the affected files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant context difference is retry state: parallel lost packaging progress across retry boundaries, while serial preserved context locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation followed the synthesized spec and wrote six files with Format, ProgressBuilder, ProgressTracker, and root test5.rs, then verified equality.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented similar module files but with builder.rs/tracker.rs names, hit rustc import and dead-code issues, edited them, and passed local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths reached a passing artifact; serial's implementation evolved in-place, while parallel used analysis/spec handoff before a single implementation child wrote /output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Analysis and implementation results were returned inside the workflow, but the workflow was killed during verifier phase before aggregate workflow result, fix/critic, or final parent response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its local loop and returned a final answer after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel artifact lifecycle completed enough for evaluation, but workflow/user-report lifecycle remained unfinished; serial closed both artifact and response lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel avoided concurrent /output writes by assigning the implementer exclusive ownership; other analysts and verifiers used /tmp or read-only /output checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and edited the same project files itself, with no concurrent actors and no shared-state collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No harmful shared-state collision occurred in either run; parallel had more actors but kept final implementation writes centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation performed rustc/cargo and byte-equality checks and official evaluation passed, but planned verifier aggregation and critic did not finish.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran unit tests, rustc/cargo builds, byte comparisons across argument sets, dependency checks, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both met official acceptance; serial had complete local closure, while parallel had successful implementation checks but incomplete planned verification lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent nearly the whole 2400-second budget, stalled and retried packaging twice, then timed out with workflow status killed and empty final.txt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 518 seconds with returncode 0, final response present, and substantial remaining budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel solved the artifact but failed process closure; serial solved the artifact and closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are concordant: both parallel and serial pass 1 of 1 testcase. The substantive difference is not evaluator outcome but lifecycle cost: parallel used a multi-agent workflow that eventually produced a correct artifact but timed out before final aggregation and user response, while serial completed the entire local implementation, verification, and reporting loop.
parallel_contributors: Parallel analysts and architect produced a detailed spec, and the implementer wrote and verified a byte-identical artifact.
Packaging retry state loss and broad verifier fan-out created deadline pressure and left workflow closure incomplete.
serial_contributors: Serial preserved all findings in one context and fixed the rustc import and dead-code issues locally.
Serial completed verification and final response before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial final response admits untested choices around division by zero and defaults; official tests did not exercise them.
Parallel implementation chose a narrower spec-derived API and still passed the evaluated five-line output.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained coordination pattern is an adverse process contributor only

candidates.reason: The workflow assigned one implementer to own /output and that child wrote the complete project, so implementation was not ownerless.
Parallel did not delegate separate code components requiring reconciliation; a single implementer integrated the final module tree.
The implementer owned Cargo.toml, root test5.rs, module placement, and final binaries; final assembly was assigned and completed.
The workflow script itself owned the end-to-end stages; the issue was retry state and timeout, not a missing pipeline owner.
Implementation was staged after analysis by design, but no single mandatory serial harness or oracle gate alone blocked productive work.
The initial investigation did run before implementation, but it returned a spec that was used successfully; the adverse episode was retry state loss, not deferred investigation itself.
The indispensable implementation path had a dedicated implementer and completed; remaining deadline pressure is better explained by checkpoint-free packaging retries.
The workflow exhausted its budget, but the directly evidenced retained boundary is repeated packaging retry without checkpoint; the missing verifier aggregate is downstream of that same chain.
The packaging brief was broad, but a later retry completed it and it was not the single overbroad child left holding indispensable implementation work.
The child prompts included the task requirements, output bytes, build paths, no-dependency rule, argv behavior, and delivery constraints.
The workflow did not ask independent implementers to create interoperating components; analysis fed a single spec and a single implementer wrote all final files.
No known finding is shown as omitted from a handoff that a receiver needed; the repeated retry issue is lack of checkpoint between attempts.
The architect and implementer consumed large structured reports successfully enough to produce a passing artifact; no receiver is shown overloaded by bulk.
No child or parent consumed a superseded handoff as current; stale /tmp scratch was detected and wiped rather than used for final decisions.
The analyses contained some disagreements, but the design child explicitly resolved them into a coherent spec before implementation.
The parallel parent never made a whole-task completion claim; final.txt is empty and official pass alone cannot establish this label.

The packaging specialist was restarted after stalls with the same broad original assignment and no visible checkpoint from prior attempts; retries repeated environment checks, reference output probing, and scratch skeleton work before the final retry returned.
candidates.realized_consequence: Repeated packaging retries consumed workflow budget and contributed to the workflow being killed before verifier aggregation, fix/critic, and final response, despite the artifact passing official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: Budget exhaustion was visible, but the narrower directly fixable boundary for this repeated-work episode is missing checkpoint state on retries.

No child implementation was merged after integrated verification; the implementation preceded verifier starts and no later merge occurred.
The delegated implementation wrote directly to /output and artifact validation captured those files, so no completed implementation was omitted from the final artifact.
Verifier results were absent because the workflow was killed after retry-driven budget pressure; per taxonomy this is downstream of the retained retry chain, not a separate verifier-return label.
Packaging stalls were retried and eventually produced a result; later verifier non-completion is part of the same timeout chain and not an independent required child takeover failure.
Completed analysis, spec, packaging, and implementation results were consumed by later workflow stages; no available completed result is shown ignored at a decision point.
The parent did wait for the background workflow, but the more specific retained boundary is the checkpoint-free stalled retry chain inside that workflow.
There were no competing live implementations of overlapping final behavior; only the implementer wrote the final project files.
No two live agents edited the same final source file and no reconciliation of concurrent same-file edits is shown.
No agent replaced source produced or actively owned by another agent in the final workspace.
The rustc and cargo binaries were produced by the implementer as expected and did not overwrite another actor's deliverable.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree outputs; artifact validation found the implementer's project.
Although all actors could see /output, the workflow explicitly made verifiers read-only and gave write ownership to one implementer; no unstable final provenance occurred.
A retry noticed stale /tmp/pkgcheck scratch content and wiped it; no actor consumed another actor's temporary artifact as stable input for the final solution.
